text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- More then 50,000 Serb soldiers were killed in the Bosnian war, the Bosnian Croat militia lost about 25,000 soldiers while the mainly Moslem Bosnian army lost 30,000 troops, Western military analysts say.

- Bosnian army which today celebrates its fifth aniversary has grown up into a powerful millitary factor in the Balkans and it is the best guarantee for safety of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Moslem people, commentary says.
- One of the bigest problems that the Bosnian army faces in the future is the creation of a Moslem-Croat federation military because Croats are constantly obstructing the process.
- U.S. diplomat Robert Gelbard replaces American envoy for former Yugoslavia, John Kornblum, at a ceremony in the U.S. embassy in Sarajevo.
- "I wish the echo of the Pope's visit to Sarajevo to be audible for a long time," Bosnian Cardinal Vinko Puljic says.

- Arrival of international supervisor, Robert Farrand, to disputed town of Brcko means that authority of the international community is being put into place while reducing the authority of the Serb republic, Bosnian member of the arbitration team, Cazim Sadikovic, says.
- Moslem deputy mayor of divided town of Mostar says that Mostar is now a peaceful town.

- Bosnian engineering company Unis-Holding earned a total of 55 million German marks ($32 million) in the last year. The company now has 6,000 employees working in 42 branches in the Moslem-Croat federation, officials say.

- The town of Brcko is a crisis point which could cause a conflict that would destroy current peace, but the problem is not so critical as long as NATO-led troops are here, Bosnian federation army commander-in-chief, Rasim Delic, says. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
